title: Certify all 128 signed n8 prefix maxima at 23/16 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Complete finite certificate: every one of the 128 symbols `(1, s1/8, s2/16, ..., s7/16)`, with each sign in `{-1,+1}`, has largest proper forward-prefix infinity norm exactly **23/16** under even-first triangular parity execution. All signs first attain the maximum at cut 11 and retain it through cut 21.

```text
128 distinct sign tuples
  -> exact 22-factor parity words
  -> 2,688 proper prefix matrices
  -> maximum 23/16 for every tuple
```

Brian's general theorem already gives 3/2 for tail l1=1/2. This adds the sharper complete fixed-magnitude envelope and an attaining-row argument. James Reed's individual examples retain their credit. No new kappa.

## Evidence

Before: published individual sign choices and the general 3/2 bound. After: the complete 128-symbol domain, its exact cut envelope and eight rejecting controls. The verifier imports no predecessor checker.

Local warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass, timed at 0.701 s and 0.683 s. Registered package replay, committed-byte/source-history checks, deterministic export integrity and an isolated optimized Git-free export replay pass. Both arithmetic modes produce certificate SHA256 `ee323f6e58fb4a3c802cc53b413d097502ede14e12454dd35308e5268584c1a2`. Receipts are generated and bound to all package source hashes.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/triangular-parity-sign-cube/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/triangular-parity-sign-cube/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/triangular-parity-sign-cube
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/triangular-parity-sign-cube --check-source-history
```

Add `--details` to a direct verifier command to enumerate all 128 sign tuples and 21 rational norms each. Expected status: `PASS_TRIANGULAR_PARITY_SIGN_CUBE`, with `symbols=128`, `proper_prefixes=2688`, and `maximum_distribution={"23/16":128}`. Standard-library CPython 3.12 suffices; the absolute interpreter path identifies the local environment.

## Limitations

This is a complete finite certificate for one fixed magnitude family and serial even-first macro order. It does not prove a sharper bound for other dimensions, magnitudes, coefficient-box interiors or child interleavings. Gate-level rounding, generator normalization, the Gaussian caller, tape costs and the p^100 precision ledger are unrun obligations. No supplier admission, selected-frontier change or multiplication theorem is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Does 23/16 remain exact for this finite family under every legal child interleaving? First enumerate pairs of child cuts; this certificate fixes even-first execution.
- Is there an analytic coefficient-sensitive envelope explaining the 1/16 improvement? Start with the support omitted by the unfinished root left shear; no such formula is supplied here.

Brian's merged forward-bound and four-cut packages, Vlado Vojdanovski's retained compiler, Cinna Davis's caller and Ryanson Jonathan's error-ledger context are pinned or credited in the README. The scope changes the all-size audit card to a finite precision side result.
